mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising the cost of capital and depressing corporate earnings growth, which in turn leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.5% median) during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation exceeds 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-2% median) during triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate when GDP growth is accompanied by strong productivity gains.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate above 4% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending power and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 4% in one month after being below 4% the prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1% median) during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when wage growth is accelerating.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months indicates supply-side stress, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.2% median) during triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate when energy prices are falling sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary and price pressures, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 12-mo avg AND CPIAUCSL > 12-mo avg in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-1.5% median) during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when credit spreads are collapsing.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-mo moving average for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>0.8% median) during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when mortgage rates are rising sharply.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) within the same month indicates a statistical artifact of labor force reclassification rather than genuine job creation, which historically coincides with market uncertainty and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while UNRATE also increases in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative (<-0.5% median) during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of major labor law changes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) for six consecutive months signals strengthening household balance sheets and higher consumption potential, which supports corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS increases for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (>1.2% median) during triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when consumer confidence is falling sharply.
